title: Domain Settings: Privacy, Locks, Nameservers and DNSSEC for Domain Registrations
content:
## Product terms — settings on Domain Registrations

**S1. When settings may change.** A settings change may be made only while the domain status is active, on hold or grace. The status is read from the system record of the domain before the change.

**S2. WHOIS privacy.** WHOIS privacy may be switched on only where the TLD offers privacy, and it is billed at the TLD's annual privacy price. .us registrations may never carry privacy, and .ca registrations rely on the registry's own disclosure rules.

**S3. Registry lock.** Registry lock may be ordered only where the TLD offers it, and it is billed at the TLD's annual registry lock fee per year, aligned to the domain's expiry date.

**S4. While a registry lock is in force.** The registrar transfer lock stays on, and no change of registrant, nameserver change or authorisation code is possible. Releasing the lock takes the TLD's registry lock release business days, counted Monday to Friday excluding US federal holidays, from the registrant's authorised request.

**S5. Registrar transfer lock.** The registrar transfer lock is on by default where the TLD's registrar lock default is Yes, and the registrant may switch it off or on at any time outside a registry lock.

**S6. Nameservers and DNSSEC.** Nameserver changes take effect at the registry immediately, and DNSSEC may be enabled only on Harborline DNS where the TLD supports DNSSEC.

### Settings at a glance

| Setting | Condition in these terms |
|---|---|
| auto-renew, privacy, registrar lock, registry lock, nameservers | domain active, on hold or grace (S1) |
| privacy on | TLD offers privacy; never on .us (S2) |
| registry lock ordered | TLD offers registry lock; annual fee aligned to expiry (S3) |
| registrar lock switched off | no registry lock in force (S4, S5) |
| nameserver change | no registry lock in force (S4) |
| DNSSEC | Harborline DNS, TLD supports DNSSEC (S6) |

### Hypothetical release count

A registry lock release requested on a Thursday under a two-business-day release, with no federal holiday in between, counts the Friday and the Monday as its two business days.
